title: When Construction Runs Late: Builder Delay Rights Under Your Home Purchase Agreement
content:
**Your completion dates.** Your Home Purchase Agreement states a contract completion date at signing. Each construction stage update refreshes the estimated completion date; the contract completion date stated at signing never changes.

**Your right to cancel for builder delay.** A cancellation request with basis builder delay is honored only when the home is not complete and the request is received no earlier than the collection's builder delay tolerance (calendar days) after the contract completion date. Counting starts the day after the contract completion date, and the request may be honored on the last counted day.

What decides it is on Calloway's records: the contract completion date and construction stage on the agreement, and the received date on your cancellation request.

**What you receive.** On such a cancellation every deposit is refunded, the lot premium deposit and transferred reservation funds included, and no mutual release fee is charged.

**Your rate lock.** Where the collection provides that Calloway pays rate lock extensions caused by builder delay, rate lock extension charges caused by a builder delay are borne by Calloway and waived on the lock.

## Both sides of the threshold (hypothetical dates)

A contract completion date of 1 June and a builder delay tolerance of 120 days put the last counted day on 29 September.

| Request received | Home complete? | Builder-delay request |
|---|---|---|
| 28 September | No | Not honored: received earlier than 120 days after the contract completion date |
| 29 September | No | Honored |
| 15 October | No | Honored |
| 15 October | Yes | Not honored: the home is complete |

With a 150-day tolerance and the same contract completion date, the first day a builder-delay request may be honored is 29 October.

A later estimated completion date does not move the count: it always runs from the contract completion date stated at signing.
